# Best Practices for Citation-Backed Research Using Agentic AI

How a single human operator using an LLM-backed CLI agent can produce verifiable, auditable research documents. Synthesized from 37 sources including peer-reviewed papers, production system documentation, government studies, and empirical benchmarks.

## Key Finding

Agentic research works not because agents are reliable, but because the methodology makes unreliability visible. Hallucination rates span 3-69% depending on context — from 3.1% for grounded summarization to 69% for ungrounded citation generation. The methodology compensates through structural separation: writer agents, verifier agents, and a human operator occupy distinct roles with no shared context between writer and verifier.

## Decision Framework

1. **Use 3-5 parallel agents** for research — more agents increase coordination failures without proportional quality gains [Google Research: +81% on parallelizable tasks, -70% on sequential]
2. **Require inline citations** in all agent output — forces the "dual-error" mechanism where fabrication requires both a false claim and a false citation [Microsoft]
3. **Separate writer and verifier roles** with no shared context — a 770M parameter model can match GPT-4 fact-checking at 400× lower cost when given source material [MiniCheck]
4. **Plan for 20-30% source inaccessibility** — provide 2-3 candidate sources per data point; never silently drop failed fetches [Pew: 25% of 2013-2023 pages gone]
5. **Gate irreversible decisions only** — plan approval and final publication need human review; source discovery and data extraction can proceed autonomously
6. **Avoid expert persona prompts** — they reduce factual accuracy by 3.6 percentage points on MMLU [PRISM, USC 2026]

## Methodology

6 discovery agents dispatched in parallel, URL manifests aggregated, sources batch-fetched, reference files composed, deliverable written, two independent verification agents audited the output. Produced on 2026-03-29 using the cited-research methodology.
